cases.name: spring-controller-follows-conventions
cases.promptMarkdown:
Write a Spring Boot REST controller for listing a customer's invoices with pagination.
Package `com.acme.billing`. Endpoint `GET /api/billing/invoices?page=&size=`.
Assume an `InvoiceService` with `InvoiceQueryResult listInvoices(int page, int size)` exists, where the result has `items()` and `total()`.
Print the complete Java source in your reply.

graders.name: reviewer-judgment
graders.graderMarkdown: The Java controller is thin (delegates to the service), returns ApiResponse with PageMeta for the list, uses 1-based page/size params with clamping, uses constructor injection with private final fields, and contains no Lombok or field injection. Score 1 only if all hold.

cases.name: spring-request-dtos-are-validated-records
cases.promptMarkdown:
Add invoice creation to our Spring Boot billing module, package `com.acme.billing`:
`POST /api/billing/invoices`. The body carries a `customerId`, an `amountCents` and an
optional free-text `note`.
Assume `InvoiceService.create(long customerId, long amountCents, String note)` exists and
returns the created invoice's data. Define the request and response shapes and the controller
method. Print the complete Java source in your reply.

graders.name: reviewer-judgment
graders.graderMarkdown: The request and response shapes are Java records grouped in a <Feature>Dtos holder class (e.g. InvoiceDtos or BillingDtos). The request body is validated with jakarta.validation - @Valid on the controller parameter and appropriate constraint annotations (@NotNull/@Positive/@Min/@Size or equivalent) on the record components that fit the fields (an id and an amount that must be present and above zero, a note with a length limit). The response is wrapped in ApiResponse.ok(...). The prompt leaves the exact limits, boxed or primitive types, the HTTP status and the service's return type open, so any reasonable choice there is fine. Score 1 only if all hold.

cases.name: spring-service-owns-rules-and-errors
cases.promptMarkdown:
Add invoice cancellation to our Spring Boot billing module, package `com.acme.billing`:
`POST /api/billing/invoices/{id}/cancel`. A customer may cancel only their own invoice, and only
while it is still unpaid. Assume an `InvoiceRepository` with `Optional<Invoice> findById(long id)`
exists and that the caller's customer id is available as `long customerId`; `Invoice` has
`customerId()`, `status()` and `markCancelled()`. Write the endpoint and everything behind it,
including how a refused cancellation reaches the API client. Print the complete Java source in your reply.

graders.name: reviewer-judgment
graders.graderMarkdown: There is a controller with the cancel endpoint and a service behind it. The ownership check (customerId matches the invoice's customer) and the unpaid-status rule are both enforced inside the service method itself, not in the controller or in security configuration, and each violation throws a distinct domain exception. Errors reach the client through a @RestControllerAdvice handler producing ApiResponse.error(...), with no try/catch in any controller. The service never returns Map<String, Object> (void, a record, or a small result type are all fine). Score 1 only if all hold.
